narrative.overview: Dark Pawns is a dark-fantasy world first built in 1994 and left for dead around 2010. This site is what you find when you pull that world off a dusty shelf: a warm, yellowed mass-market paperback with a newspaper folded inside it, still faintly warm, still running. The whole system points at one feeling: an archive of a game that refuses to die. The look is cream paper and charcoal ink, structured with the stark hairline logic of a broadsheet and marked with a single oxblood accent used like a librarian's stamp. No gradients, no shadows, no glows; depth comes from the weight of a rule and the faint shift between two creams. The primary visitor is a human player; agents and researchers are first-class in the game but not the headline of the site.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper, charcoal ink, one oxblood stamp
Flat by physical law: hairline rules and tonal cream layering, never shadow
Serif for reading and headlines; monospace only for game and machine chrome; no sans-serif
Sharp corners (2px maximum); the page is printed, not rounded
Sourced or silent: nothing asserted without a primary source

rules.name: The One Oxblood Rule
rules.body: Oxblood is the only accent and appears on roughly 10% or less of any screen. Its rarity is the point; a second accent or an oxblood fill breaks the system.

rules.name: The Paper-Not-White Rule
rules.body: Pure #FFFFFF and #000000 never appear except the CRT canvas at /play (#0a0908). Every surface is Paper or Paper-Deep; every black is Ink.

rules.name: The Two-Serif-and-a-Terminal Rule
rules.body: Display serif for headings and wordmark, body serif for reading, monospace only for game and machine chrome. No sans-serif, and no font loaded that isn't used.

rules.name: The Flat-Ink Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and on interaction. Raised elements get a rule or a shift to Paper-Deep, never a shadow.

rules.name: The 2px Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounder than 2px, except a true circle for a genuine status dot or avatar.

rules.name: The Sourced-or-Silent Rule
rules.body: No claim, number, date, or lore appears on any surface unless it traces to a primary source. When there is no source, the surface stays silent rather than plausible.

rules.name: The Archive-Is-The-Pitch Rule
rules.body: Marketing surfaces persuade through the depth, age, and specificity of the world, never through product-launch conventions.

dos: Do lead with the specificity of the world; the archive is the pitch
Do keep Oxblood rare and every black as Ink
Do convey depth with rules and cream layering only
Do write all public copy in brand-voice.md Layer 3 (Frontline's Mythic Admin register)
Do treat the human player as the primary visitor in every layout and hierarchy decision
Do keep monospace for game and machine chrome exclusively
donts: Don't use em-dashes in UI copy: headlines, buttons, labels, nav, captions
Don't use section-numbering eyebrows or decorative colophons; the FILED UNDER line is banned
Don't build three-equal-card feature rows; use asymmetric or two-column editorial layouts
Don't build fake terminal or dashboard UIs; the only real terminal is the game client at /play
Don't use gradients, box-shadows, glows, or any border radius over 2px
Don't use pure white/black (except the CRT canvas), sans-serif fonts, or any color outside the palette
Don't use gimmicky spooky assets (bats, cobwebs, dripping-blood text, flaming dividers)
Don't adopt SaaS marketing patterns: hero-with-gradient, Get-Started funnels, pills-on-images, testimonial carousels
Don't assert any fact, stat, or lore without a primary source
